calls.title: Stephen Haw and Graham McNicoll + 4 others
calls.summary: The meeting served as an unintended onboarding session, initiated due to a Calendly scheduling issue that caused overlaps in invites. Graham McNicoll explained this to Daniel, who was unsure about his role in the discussion. Personal stories were shared, including Daniel's wedding experience and family backgrounds, helping to build rapport among participants. The conversation also touched on environmental issues like coral reef degradation and the impact of tourism, with Daniel expressing an interest in coral restoration as a career. Additionally, they humorously discussed wildlife dangers in Australia, sharing anecdotal experiences. The meeting concluded with the confirmation of future scheduling, emphasizing respect for participants' time.
calls.keywords: Onboarding, Wedding, Family Reunion, Australia, Coral Reef Restoration, Travel
calls.action_items:
**Graham McNicoll**
Review and fix legacy Calendly onboarding links to prevent unnecessary invitations (05:33)
Share recommendations for reef tours with marine biologists for Coral restoration insights, to Daniel or colleagues interested in reef ecology (14:09)

**Daniel**
Participate as an observer ('fly on the wall') for onboarding meetings only if appropriate, otherwise opt out (06:38)
Follow up with Ashley as scheduled, and continue planning Hawaii trip with remote work logistics for his wife (20:31)

calls.title: Stephen Haw and Graham McNicoll + 4 others
calls.summary: The team discussed a notable mismatch in experiment metrics, particularly in visits and conversions. Stephen reported 10,100 visits, while marketing claimed 18,923, leading to concerns over the reliability of data. Conversion tracking also revealed discrepancies, with only 54 internal conversions versus 2,972 reported externally. Graham clarified the primary conversion metric and highlighted issues with using Device IDs due to blank User IDs. A plan was established to engage the Growth Book engineering team for further diagnostics, with a focus on firing explicit page view events to improve data integrity. Collaborative troubleshooting between the frontend, backend, and engineering teams was emphasized to restore trust in experiment data.
calls.keywords: GrowthBook, Conversion Tracking, Data Discrepancies, Event Firing, Page View Pixel, SQL Query
calls.action_items:
**Stephen Haw**
Implement explicit page view event firing on all pages and validate tracking improvements (20:19)
Coordinate with marketing and internal team to create a new test experiment reflecting this update for accurate baseline (26:01)
Keep GrowthBook team updated on test experiment outcomes and any anomalies detected (26:28)

**Jay (Jacob Whittaker)**
Assist Stephen in deploying test experiments with recommended tracking changes (26:17)
Continue troubleshooting User ID issue and support SQL queries and data verification efforts (11:08)

**Graham McNicoll**
Review recorded meeting and internal engineering team to identify causes of data discrepancies and event loss (24:52)
Follow up with Stephen and Jay with findings and possible technical resolutions (25:32)
